predecessors.name: Kingdom of Brittany
predecessors.text: Brittany, Norse-occupied from 919 and reconquered by Alan II; the duchy page's infobox lists 'Brittany' and 'Viking Brittany' as predecessors

successors.name: Kingdom of France
successors.text: the duchy united with France: 'The Estates proclaimed union in 1532'; the infobox gives 'Union with France: 13 August 1547'

ledger.x: 939: Alan II, Barbetorte, wins at Trans-la-Forêt and founds the duchy.
960: Nantes leaves the ducal line (bridging a silence).
990: Conan I takes Nantes and styles himself duke.
990: the House of Rennes takes the duchy with Conan I ('House of Rennes, Conan I: Became duke in 990'); the state, its colour and its land continue.
1066: the House of Cornouaille takes the duchy.
1158: Conan IV gives Nantes to Henry II.
1164: Henry II seizes lands on the Normandy border.
1166: Henry II invades and takes the duchy under his guardianship.
1181: Geoffrey marries Constance and the duchy passes to them.
1185: Nantes returns to the duchy.
1213: the House of Dreux takes the duchy.
1341: the Breton war of succession begins.
1343: an English garrison holds Brest.
1365: the war ends at Guérande.
1365: the House of Montfort takes the duchy.
1378: Charles V tries to annex the duchy.
1379: the Breton barons recall John IV.
1397: Brest is recovered from the English.
1487: the French army enters Brittany.
1488: Saint-Aubin-du-Cormier ends the war.
1488: French garrisons hold the pledged towns.
1491: Rennes falls and Anne marries Charles VIII.
1532: the Estates of Brittany proclaim the union with France.

wars.name: War of the Breton Succession
wars.outcome: Montfort victory: Charles of Blois killed at Auray on 29 September 1364; the First Treaty of Guérande of 12 April 1365 established John of Montfort as duke, with Joan of Penthièvre giving up her rights.

wars.name: Mad War
wars.outcome: French victory at Saint-Aubin-du-Cormier (28 July 1488); the Treaty of Sablé (20 August 1488) makes Francis II the king's vassal and pledges the conquered territories to France; Rennes falls in 1491 and Anne marries Charles VIII.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey draws the duchy's frontier in any page opened; the marches with Normandy, Maine and Anjou are feudal and approximate.
